entry.title: AI Across the Curriculum: Tandon Forum

link.title: AI Across the Curriculum: Tandon Forum

entry.content:
Building a Human-Centered Approach to AI in Engineering Education

On October 2, NYU Tandon hosted AI Across the Curriculum: A Tandon Forum, marking the launch of a school-wide initiative led by R/AI Director Julia Stoyanovich, Associate Dean of AI Initiatives. The initiative has a clear goal: to build a human-centered infrastructure that first assesses what faculty and students need, and then addresses those needs.

The work is participatory by design: the people a policy or course will serve help shape it. In Spring 2026, every Tandon department examined how AI is affecting its courses and developed its own strategy. Across the school, one concern stood out: not cheating, but the loss of learning when students submit correct work they do not understand.

Over the summer, three faculty working groups—Policy, Survey, and Resources—translated departmental strategies into shared tools, including adaptable AI-use policy language, a school-wide student survey, and a repository of teaching materials. Students also joined the deliberation, with 240 students in two pilot courses debating and voting on their own course AI policies.

The forum brought together faculty and students to share these developments, discuss emerging priorities, and help shape the next phase of the initiative. Through presentations, a student panel, and interactive breakout sessions, participants explored how Tandon can respond to AI’s impact on teaching and learning.

entry.title: Who’s Responsible for AI? A Conversation with Julia Stoyanovich and Paul Ford

link.title: Who’s Responsible for AI? A Conversation with Julia Stoyanovich and Paul Ford

entry.content:
On September 15, Julia Stoyanovich joined Paul Ford, co-founder of Aboard, for a conversation about what it means to build and use AI responsibly, and who gets to decide what “responsible” means.

The discussion explored who bears responsibility when AI systems cause harm, the “magical thinking” surrounding AI, and the different perspectives technologists and policymakers bring to AI governance. Julia also shared what responsible AI can look like in practice for companies developing and deploying AI systems.

Learn more about the event.
entry.summary: A conversation hosted by Aboard on responsibility and AI governance

entry.title: R/AI Research for Ukrainian Scholars – Fall 2026 Open House

link.title: R/AI Research for Ukrainian Scholars – Fall 2026 Open House

entry.content:
On September 9, RAI for Ukraine kicked off the 2026–27 academic year with its annual Open House, welcoming a new cohort of research fellows and hearing from new and returning mentors about the projects they will lead this year. This fall, 32 research fellows will work with 28 mentors on 15 research projects.

As the program enters its fifth year, its achievements since launching in 2022 reflect the growth of an international research community:

  • 141 research fellows from 19 Ukrainian universities, including this year’s cohort
  • 81 mentors representing 40 academic institutions across 13 countries
  • 57 research projects completed
  • 24 peer-reviewed publications to date, with several more in the pipeline

🎥 Missed the Open House? Watch the full recording on YouTube.

🌐 Learn more about the program: RAI for Ukraine

entry.title: What Everyone Should Know About AI | Julia Stoyanovich on ease

link.title: What Everyone Should Know About AI | Julia Stoyanovich on ease

entry.content:
“The question isn’t whether machines can be conscious. It’s where these systems belong in our lives, and whether they’re doing what we want them to do.” — Julia Stoyanovich

On May 29, Julia Stoyanovich joined host Nailea Devora on an episode of ease, “What Everyone Should Know About AI,” to break down what artificial intelligence actually is, how it works, and why understanding it matters.

From robot vacuums and chess to ELIZA, the first therapy chatbot, and her grandfather calculating Sputnik trajectories, Julia used stories and humor to take the magic out of AI and remind us that we are ultimately in control.

🎥 Watch on YouTube or 🎧 listen on Spotify.
entry.summary: Julia Stoyanovich joins Nailea Devora on ease to discuss AI and why understanding it matters.

entry.title: R/AI Research for Ukrainian Scholars – Spring 2026 Showcase

link.title: R/AI Research for Ukrainian Scholars – Spring 2026 Showcase

entry.content:
Another Semester of the Responsible AI for Ukraine Program Wraps Up with a Project Showcase!

On May 8, R/AI hosted the Spring 2026 #RAIforUkraine Project Showcase, bringing together research fellows, mentors, partners, and supporters from across 12 countries. Eleven teams presented research projects spanning our core themes—algorithmic fairness, interpretability, privacy, data management for ML, and evaluation—alongside emerging directions such as multilingual misinformation detection, AI-powered species identification in underwater imagery, and physics-informed generative AI for the design of next-generation catalysts.

The showcase highlighted the progress made over the semester, with presentations covering both current results and publications they aim to pursue. Collectively, these projects reflected one of the most diverse portfolios we have seen to date. A select group of students demonstrating strong progress or particularly promising results will continue their work in Summer 2026 with support from program stipends.

🎥 If you missed the live event, you can now watch the recording on our YouTube channel.

entry.title: Julia Stoyanovich delivers a keynote at Fordham University

link.title: Julia Stoyanovich delivers a keynote at Fordham University

entry.content:
On April 29, Julia Stoyanovich delivered a keynote at Fordham University’s 2026 Graduate Research Celebration, an expanded university-wide event showcasing the breadth, rigor, and impact of graduate scholarship across disciplines.

Her address, “The Joys of Doing, Learning, Being in the Age of AI,” explored the connections between three aspects of her work that bring her joy—research, teaching, and policymaking—and the broader mission of the Center, which spans technical AI research, education and training, and the development of accountability and governance frameworks around AI.

Moving between philosophy, public education, technical research, and policy, Julia reflected on what should remain deeply human in the age of AI: the experience of learning, creating, questioning, and taking responsibility for the systems that shape our lives.
